# Fieldwork practices

Fieldwork is a collection of engineering practices. Its caller sketch asks the agent to write two or three realistic examples of another part of the program using a proposed interface, including expected results and failures, before implementing it. The developer reviews the examples in the design discussion. The agent derives the public operations and data types from those examples. This can expose a design that forces every caller to coordinate internal steps. It is not a requirement to implement a throwaway framework or have multiple agents compete.

Fieldwork's app recipe records the actual startup command, a check that startup has reached a usable state, isolated sample data, the steps and stable controls for exercising a feature, its expected visible result, and cleanup. The author runs the recipe before saving it. Later agents follow the saved instructions and update them when the app changes. The benefit is avoiding repeated discovery of how to operate the same app; the cost is maintaining instructions that can become stale.

Fieldwork's regression pass checks affected behavior and dependencies and directly exercises the changed user operation. Its performance checklist calls for realistic input, counts of successful operations and errors, alternating repeated measurements of old and new versions, and confirmation that the timed work actually completed.
sources/mosaic-workflow.md:
# Mosaic's current workflow

Mosaic is a desktop note editor. Agents discuss requirements, public interfaces, and important architecture choices with the owner during planning, then implement, validate, and review. There is no specific instruction to write caller examples before choosing an interface.

Validation already runs affected regression tests, considers dependencies, and directly exercises changed user behavior. It also requires before/after measurement of the complete user operation for performance claims, using realistic data, repeated alternating runs, completed-work counts, and errors.

The repository has a documented startup command, but no maintained feature-driving recipes or sample workspace. Recent agents each rediscovered how to launch an isolated instance, create a note, save it, restart, and confirm the saved note reopened. A verification recipe would belong with the project's existing agent skills and would be consulted during validation. The owner has not approved any Fieldwork adoption.
